Through formal partnerships and scheduled access, the CEC provides a stable, trusted venue that reconnects community life to an accessible, multi-use facility.

Description: An annual fall festival at the Cathedral of Learning featuring Slovak food, music, dance, storytelling, and hands-on craft demonstrations led by artisans and elders. Organized with university faculty, student groups, and community volunteers, it offers intergenerational activities, language and genealogy sessions, and vendor booths that strengthen cultural pride and cross-community connections.

Description: The Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy trains volunteers to adopt and regularly maintain specific park sites, providing instruction in tool safety and hands-on upkeep techniques. Volunteers conduct ongoing maintenance such as trail repairs, boardwalk and fence fixes, invasive removal, and cleanups—reducing municipal maintenance costs while cultivating long-term stewardship and strong community connections.

Name: Vacant to Vibrant
Description: This initiative provides short-term access and support for entrepreneurs and nonprofits to use vacant downtown Erie storefronts for pop-up retail, community programming, and special events. By rotating participants and measuring traffic and sales, it recreates multi-use community functions in empty spaces while generating data and visibility that help property owners transition spaces to longer-term, mission-aligned tenants.

Name: Volunteer-Run Venue Operations
Description: The Mr. Roboto Project is a cooperatively run, all-ages community venue where volunteers coordinate bookings, staff the door, run shows, and maintain the space. Volunteer stewards manage the event calendar, welcome attendees, enforce safety policies, and handle day-of logistics, creating a reliable, accessible place for diverse community events and meetings.

Name: Welcoming Pittsburgh
Description: The City’s Welcoming Pittsburgh initiative partners with neighborhood groups and resident volunteers to host newcomer orientations, welcome events, and peer connections that introduce people to their local community. Through ambassador-style outreach and invitations to civic and cultural gatherings, the program helps new residents quickly meet long-time Pittsburghers and build trust in neighborhood institutions.
Organization: City of Pittsburgh – Office of Immigrant and Refugee Affairs

Name: Wilkins School Community Center
Description: Wilkins School Community Center is a resident-led nonprofit hub in a former school that offers low-cost classes in arts, dance, fitness, and community programs, plus affordable room rentals for meetings and clubs. The center welcomes people of all ages and backgrounds, providing neutral space for gatherings, workshops, and recreational activities. As a community-run facility, it functions as an inclusive alternative to membership-limited or politically affiliated clubs.

Name: Wilkins School Community Center (WSCC)
Description: WSCC is a community-run center in a former neighborhood school that rents classrooms, halls, and meeting rooms for clubs, training sessions, family celebrations, support groups, and civic gatherings. Supported by members, volunteers, and a community board, the organization keeps rates affordable and channels proceeds back into maintenance and programming, giving local users an ongoing voice in operations.

Description: WorkLaunch is an annual series co-presented by JFCS Career Development Center and Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh that delivers free workshops, employer panels, resume clinics, and job fairs at library branches across Allegheny County. By bringing adult education and hiring events directly into neighborhood libraries and co-hosting them with workforce agencies and local employers, it steadily activates library spaces and demonstrates community value to garner public support.

Name: Workforce & Education Committee
Description: The Beaver County Chamber’s Workforce & Education Committee functions as a community-employer liaison forum where manufacturers, training providers, and residents surface local needs and jointly plan solutions. It hosts employer listening sessions and neighborhood hiring events, and works with plant management to pilot practical steps like neighborhood-based recruitment, shift adjustments to fit transit and childcare realities, and coordinated transportation options for cross-county commuters.

Name: Workforce Development & Community Outreach
Description: Mon Valley Initiative blends remote coaching, virtual workshops, and online case-management with frequent pop-up hiring events and neighborhood meetings hosted at partner sites throughout the Mon Valley. Name: Workplace & Pop-Up Farmers Markets
Description: Farm to Table Buy Local organizes on-site pop-up markets at employers and community hubs across the Pittsburgh region, bringing local farmers and food producers directly to workers. These pop-ups are scheduled around shift changes and lunch/dinner breaks so commuters and shift workers can conveniently shop for fresh, local food right outside their workplaces, aligning with the solution’s emphasis on evening/early-morning access.

Organization: Farm to Table Buy Local (a program of American HealthCare Group)

Name: Y on the Fly
Description: Y on the Fly is the YMCA of Greater Pittsburgh’s mobile program that brings portable equipment, music, and activity guides to parks, school yards, and community lots for pop-up clubs focused on fitness, games, and enrichment. Staff and volunteers host recurring sessions across neighborhoods, turning underused spaces into rotating, low-barrier gathering places for all ages.
